title: 2015 AMC 10A Problem 15
statement: Consider the set of all fractions \(\dfrac{x}{y},\) where \(x\) and \(y\) are relatively prime positive integers. How many of these fractions have the property that if both numerator and denominator are increased by \(1,\) the value of the fraction is increased by \(10\%?\)

solutions.text:
The condition is \[\frac{x+1}{y+1}=\frac{11}{10}\cdot\frac{x}{y}.\] Cross-multiplying gives \(10y(x+1)=11x(y+1)\), or \(xy+11x-10y=0\).

Factoring by grouping after subtracting \(110\) gives \[(x-10)(y+11)=-110.\] Since \(x,y\) are positive, the useful negative factor pairs are \((-1,110)\), \((-2,55)\), and \((-5,22)\), producing \((x,y)=(9,99),(8,44),(5,11)\).

Only \(\frac{5}{11}\) has relatively prime numerator and denominator, so exactly one fraction works.

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Turn the fraction condition into a factorization
Only negative factor pairs with \(y+11>11\) can work
